record.paper_title: Some open problems of Ramsey minimal graphs.
record.original_question: Let F, G, and H be non-empty graphs, and write F → (G, H) to mean that every red-blue coloring of the edges of F contains either a red copy of G or a blue copy of H. A graph F is Ramsey (G, H)-minimal if F → (G, H) but, for every edge e of F, the graph F − e fails to satisfy F − e → (G, H). Let ℜ(G, H) denote the set of all Ramsey (G, H)-minimal graphs. For each integer n ≥ 6, classify all graphs in ℜ(2K2, Pn), where 2K2 is the matching consisting of two disjoint edges and Pn is the path graph on n vertices.

evidence.quote: F, G, and H, say that F → (G, H) if whenever the edges of F are 2-colored, say with red and blue, there is either a red copy of G or a blue copy of H. A graph F is called Ramsey (G, H)-minimal if F → (G, H) but for any edge e ∈ E(F), we have (F - e) ↛ (G, H). The set of all Ramsey (G, H)-minimal graphs, the topic of this note, is denoted by ℜ(G, H).
For each n ≥ 6, characterize the graphs in ℜ(2K2, Pn).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let F, G, and H be non-empty finite simple graphs. Write F → (G, H) to mean that for every red–blue coloring of the edges of F, the graph F contains either a red subgraph isomorphic to G or a blue subgraph isomorphic to H. A graph F is called Ramsey (G, H)-minimal if F → (G, H) and, for every edge e ∈ E(F), the graph F − e satisfies F − e ↛ (G, H). Let ℜ(G, H) denote the class of all Ramsey (G, H)-minimal graphs (up to isomorphism).

Let 2K₂ denote the graph consisting of two disjoint edges (a matching on four vertices), and let Pₙ denote the path on n vertices.

For each integer n ≥ 6, determine (i.e., give a complete classification of, up to isomorphism) all graphs that belong to ℜ(2K₂, Pₙ).
artifact.status_search_result: Complete characterizations of ℜ(2K₂, Pₙ) appear in the literature only for small n (notably n = 3, 4, 5), and partial structural results are known for general n (e.g., 2Pₙ is the only disconnected member, and no tree belongs to the class). No complete classification for n ≥ 6 was located, so the problem appears to be open.

status_evidence.title: Ramsey Minimal Graphs for 2K2 versus Pn
status_evidence.snippet: Investigates members of R(2K2, Pn) for n ≥ 3, proving 2Pn is the only disconnected graph in this set and no tree is a member; complete characterizations given for n = 4 and 5.
status_evidence.claim: Only partial results and small-n characterizations are known; the general case for n ≥ 6 remains uncharacterized.

status_evidence.title: On Ramsey (mK2, bPn)-minimal Graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Studies generalizations of Ramsey (2K2, Pn)-minimal graphs, indicating the full classification for paths is not yet completed for general n.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent work continues to address the family, suggesting the full characterization for n ≥ 6 is open.
